problem_en: Three workers A, B, and C can complete a task. A and B together take 10 days, while B and C together take 15 days. If A works for 2 days, then B works for 4 days, and finally C finishes the remaining work in 10 days, find the time taken by A alone to complete the entire task.
problem_hi: तीन कर्मचारी A, B, और C एक कार्य पूरा कर सकते हैं। A और B मिलकर 10 दिन लेते हैं, जबकि B और C मिलकर 15 दिन लेते हैं। यदि A 2 दिन काम करता है, फिर B 4 दिन काम करता है, और अंत में C शेष कार्य को 10 दिन में पूरा करता है, तो अकेले A द्वारा पूरे कार्य को पूरा करने में लिया गया समय ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: Three workers A, B, and C can complete a task. A and B together 10 days lete hain, whereas B and C together 15 days lete hain. Agar A 2 days kaam karta hai, phir B 4 days kaam karta hai, and finally C finishes the remaining work in 10 days, calculate the time taken by A alone to complete the task.
problem_hg_065: A aur B milkar task 10 days mein khatam karte hain, par B aur C ko 15 days lagte hain. Pehle A ne 2 days kaam kiya, phir B ne 4 days work kiya, aur baaki kaam C ne 10 days mein wrap up kiya. Bataiye A akela full work kitne time mein finish karega?
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Let efficiencies be a, b, c. Given a+b = 1/10 and b+c = 1/15.
Step 2: Total work done: 2a + 4b + 10c = 1. Rewrite as 2(a+b) + 2(b+c) + 8c = 1.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The word 'baaki' (remaining) requires the LLM to correctly group the previous work segments (2a and 4b) and subtract from the whole, but the phrasing 'phir B ne' often leads models to assume sequential non-overlapping timeframes which must be algebraically decomposed into common pairs (a+b) and (b+c).
why_hard: Requires decomposing individual work periods into given joint rate pairs to solve a system with more variables than equations.

problem_en: Efficiency of P is 200% more than Q. P works for 15 days and leaves. The remaining work is finished by Q in 30 days. If they work together, how many days will they take to complete the work?
problem_hi: P की कार्यक्षमता Q से 200% अधिक है। P 15 दिनों तक कार्य करता है और चला जाता है। शेष कार्य Q द्वारा 30 दिनों में पूरा किया जाता है। यदि वे एक साथ कार्य करते हैं, तो वे कार्य को पूरा करने में कितने दिन लेंगे?
problem_hg_030: Efficiency of P is 200% more than Q. P works for 15 days and leaves. Baaki work Q finishes in 30 days. Agar dono saath kaam karein, toh task kitne days mein complete hoga?
problem_hg_065: P ki efficiency Q se 200% zyada hai. P ne 15 days work kiya aur withdraw kar liya. Baaki bacha kaam Q ne 30 din mein finish kiya. Saath milkar kaam kitne din mein niptega?
solution_steps_en: Step 1: P = Q + 200% of Q = 3Q. Ratio of efficiency P:Q = 3:1.
Step 2: Total work = 15P + 30Q. Since P=3Q, Total work = 15(3Q) + 30Q = 45Q + 30Q = 75Q.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The trap '200% zyada' (200% more) is often misinterpreted by LLMs as '200% of' (i.e., twice as efficient), whereas it actually means three times as efficient (100% + 200%).
why_hard: LLMs frequently fail the 200% more vs 200% of distinction in code-mixed contexts.

problem_en: A can do a job in 40 days. He worked for 10 days and then B alone finished the rest in 45 days. In how many days can A and B together finish the work?
problem_hi: A एक काम को 40 दिनों में कर सकता है। उसने 10 दिनों तक काम किया और फिर B ने अकेले शेष काम 45 दिनों में पूरा किया। A और B मिलकर उस काम को कितने दिनों में पूरा कर सकते हैं?
problem_hg_030: A can do a job in 40 days. Usne 10 days kaam kiya and then B alone finished the rest in 45 days. A aur B together kitne days mein finish karenge?
problem_hg_065: A kisi kaam ko 40 din mein kar sakta hai. Sirf 10 din kaam karne ke baad A ne chhod diya, phir baaki work B ne 45 days mein finish kiya. Dono saath milkar kitne time mein kaam poora karenge?
solution_steps_en: Step 1: A's efficiency = 1/40 per day. In 10 days, A does 10/40 = 1/4 work.
Step 2: Remaining work = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4. B completes 3/4 work in 45 days.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The word 'Sirf' (only) emphasizes the 10 days but might confuse the model into thinking 10 days was the total time allotted rather than just the segment worked.
why_hard: Requires calculating a derived efficiency for worker B based on a fractional remainder of A's work.

problem_en: A team of 50 men can finish a project in 60 days. After 10 days, 10 more men join them. After another 20 days, 10 men leave. How many total days did the project take?
problem_hi: 50 पुरुषों की एक टीम 60 दिनों में एक परियोजना को पूरा कर सकती है। 10 दिनों के बाद, 10 और पुरुष उनके साथ जुड़ जाते हैं। अगले 20 दिनों के बाद, 10 पुरुष चले जाते हैं। परियोजना में कुल कितने दिन लगे?
problem_hg_030: A team of 50 men can finish a project in 60 days. 10 days ke baad, 10 more men join. After another 20 days, 10 men leave. Total project completion mein kitne din lage?
problem_hg_065: 50 men ka group project 60 days mein kar sakta hai. 10 days baad 10 aur log aa gaye. Phir 20 days baad 10 log withdraw kar gaye. Project total kitne time mein finish hua?
solution_steps_en: Step 2: Work done in first 10 days = 50 * 10 = 500. Remaining = 2500.
Step 3: 10 more join (Total 60). Work done in next 20 days = 60 * 20 = 1200. Remaining = 1300.
Step 4: 10 leave (Total 50). Time taken for remaining 1300 units = 1300 / 50 = 26 days.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The phrase '10 aur log' (10 more people) is an additive trap. LLMs sometimes reset the count to 10 or interpret it as a separate group rather than adding to the existing 50.
why_hard: Multiple workforce changes require careful tracking of the remaining work and current capacity at each stage.

problem_en: X is twice as fast as Y. Y can complete a task in 36 days. If X and Y work on alternate days starting with Y, in how many days will the task be completed?
problem_hi: X, Y से दोगुना तेज़ है। Y 36 दिनों में एक कार्य पूरा कर सकता है। यदि X और Y वैकल्पिक दिनों में काम करते हैं, जिसकी शुरुआत Y से होती है, तो कार्य कितने दिनों में पूरा होगा?
problem_hg_030: X is twice as fast as Y. Y 36 days mein task complete kar sakta hai. If X and Y work on alternate days starting with Y, kitne din lagenge?
problem_hg_065: X ki speed Y se double hai. Y akela 36 days leta hai. Agar dono alternate days pe kaam karein, pehle Y phir X, toh kaam kitne days mein wrap up hoga?
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Y's efficiency = 1/36 per day. X's efficiency = 2/36 = 1/18 per day.
Step 2: 2-day cycle (Y then X): Work done = 1/36 + 1/18 = 1/36 + 2/36 = 3/36 = 1/12.
Step 3: Number of cycles to complete work = 1 / (1/12) = 12 cycles.
Step 4: Total days = 12 cycles * 2 days/cycle = 24 days.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The 'pehle...phir' (first...then) sequence is critical. If the LLM starts with X instead of Y, the answer might differ if the total work is not a multiple of the cycle, though here it is an exact multiple.
why_hard: Alternate day logic requires calculating work per cycle and handling remainders correctly.

problem_en: A takes 10 days less than B to finish a work. If both work together, they finish in 12 days. Find the time taken by B alone.
problem_hi: A को एक काम पूरा करने में B से 10 दिन कम लगते हैं। यदि दोनों मिलकर काम करते हैं, तो वे 12 दिनों में पूरा करते हैं। अकेले B द्वारा लिया गया समय ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: A takes 10 days less than B to finish a work. Agar dono saath kaam karein, they finish in 12 days. B akela kitna time lega?
problem_hg_065: A ko kisi kaam mein B se 10 din kam lagte hain. Agar dono milkar karein toh 12 days mein kaam finish ho jayega. B akela kitne time mein 'baaki' work finish kar sakta hai (assuming he does all)?
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Let B take x days. A takes (x-10) days.
Step 5: x = 30 or x = 4. Since A takes x-10, x cannot be 4. So B = 30 days.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The addition of 'baaki' (remaining) here is a distractor. It asks for B alone to do the whole work but uses 'baaki' to imply a remainder, which could make the LLM look for a previous work stage that doesn't exist.
why_hard: Requires solving a quadratic equation and validating the physical feasibility of the roots.

problem_en: A and B can do a work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, C and A in 20 days. In how many days will C alone finish the work?
problem_hi: A और B एक काम को 12 दिनों में, B और C 15 दिनों में, C और A 20 दिनों में कर सकते हैं। C अकेले उस काम को कितने दिनों में पूरा करेगा?
problem_hg_030: A and B can do a work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, C and A in 20 days. C akela kitne din mein kaam finish karega?
problem_hg_065: A aur B milkar 12 days, B aur C milkar 15 days, aur C aur A milkar 20 days lete hain. C akela 'sirf' apna part kitne days mein finish karega?
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The word 'sirf' (only) might lead the LLM to think it needs to subtract all other contributions or interpret the question as asking for a specific fraction of the work.
why_hard: Standard cyclic work problem but easily confused when multiple pairings are introduced in Hinglish.

problem_en: 4 men and 6 women can finish a job in 8 days. 3 men and 7 women can finish it in 10 days. In how many days will 10 women finish it?
problem_hi: 4 पुरुष और 6 महिलाएँ एक काम को 8 दिनों में पूरा कर सकते हैं। 3 पुरुष और 7 महिलाएँ इसे 10 दिनों में पूरा कर सकते हैं। 10 महिलाएँ इसे कितने दिनों में पूरा करेंगी?
problem_hg_030: 4 men and 6 women can finish a job in 8 days. 3 men and 7 women can finish it in 10 days. 10 women kitne days mein finish करेंगी?
problem_hg_065: Agar 4 men aur 6 women 8 days mein kaam band kar dete hain (finish), aur 3 men aur 7 women ko 10 days lagte hain, toh 10 women 'sirf' kitne din lenge?
solution_steps_en: Step 3: Total work in terms of women: 8(4(11w) + 6w) = 8(44w + 6w) = 8 * 50w = 400 woman-days.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The phrase 'kaam band kar dete hain' (stop the work) is used here to mean 'finish the work', but an LLM might interpret it as workers quitting or the work being interrupted.
why_hard: Requires equating two different work-force compositions to find the efficiency ratio between genders.

problem_en: A can do 1/4 of a work in 10 days. B can do 40% of the work in 40 days. C can do 1/3 of the work in 13 days. Who is the fastest?
problem_hi: A एक काम का 1/4 हिस्सा 10 दिनों में कर सकता है। B उसी काम का 40% हिस्सा 40 दिनों में कर सकता है। C उसी काम का 1/3 हिस्सा 13 दिनों में कर सकता है। सबसे तेज़ कौन है?
problem_hg_030: A can do 1/4 of a work in 10 days. B can do 40% work in 40 days. C 1/3 work 13 days mein karta hai. Sabse fast kaun hai?
problem_hg_065: A 1/4 kaam 10 din mein nipatata hai. B 40% kaam 40 days mein karta hai. C ko 1/3 kaam karne mein 13 days lagte hain. Inmein se 'sabse zyada' efficient kaun hai?
solution_steps_en: Step 4: Fastest is the one with the least days: C. Wait, check A again. A is 40. C is 39. So C is fastest.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The word 'zyada' (more/most) combined with 'efficient' can be tricky. LLMs often associate 'zyada' with the larger number (100 days for B or 40 for A) instead of the smaller number (39 days for C) which indicates higher speed.
why_hard: Multiple formats (fraction, percentage) require normalization to a single metric (total days or rate).

problem_en: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours. Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty it in 6 hours. If A and B are opened for 5 hours and then C is also opened, how much more time is needed to empty the tank?
problem_hi: पाइप A एक टैंक को 12 घंटे में भर सकता है। पाइप B इसे 15 घंटे में भर सकता है। पाइप C इसे 6 घंटे में खाली कर सकता है। यदि A और B को 5 घंटे के लिए खोला जाता है और फिर C को भी खोल दिया जाता है, तो टैंक को खाली करने में कितना और समय लगेगा?
problem_hg_030: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours. Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. Pipe C can empty it in 6 hours. If A and B 5 hours ke liye open rahe and then C is also opened, tank empty hone mein kitna extra time lagega?
problem_hg_065: A 12 ghante mein fill karta hai, B 15 ghante mein. Par C use 6 ghante mein khali kar deta hai. Pehle A aur B ko 5 hours chalaya, phir C ko bhi open kar diya gaya. Tank khali hone mein 'baaki' kitna time lagega?
solution_steps_en: Step 2: In 5 hours, A and B fill: 5(1/12 + 1/15) = 5(9/60) = 5(3/20) = 3/4 of the tank.
Step 3: When C opens, net rate = 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/6 = (5 + 4 - 10)/60 = -1/60 (emptying).
Step 4: Time to empty the filled 3/4 part = (3/4) / (1/60) = 45 hours.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The passive 'khali kar diya gaya' (was opened to empty) and the word 'baaki' (remaining/extra) can confuse the model into calculating the time to fill the tank instead of emptying it, or from the start instead of after 5 hours.
why_hard: Involves negative work (drainage) and a state change after a fixed duration.

problem_en: A is twice as efficient as B and B is thrice as efficient as C. If C alone can finish the work in 120 days, in how many days will they all together finish the work?
problem_hi: A, B से दोगुना कुशल है और B, C से तीन गुना कुशल है। यदि C अकेले 120 दिनों में काम पूरा कर सकता है, तो वे सभी मिलकर कितने दिनों में काम पूरा करेंगे?
problem_hg_030: A is twice as efficient as B and B is thrice as efficient as C. Agar C akela 120 days mein finish karega, then together kitne days lagenge?
problem_hg_065: A ki efficiency B se double hai aur B ki C se triple. Agar C akela pure 120 din leta hai, toh teeno milkar 'sirf' kitne din mein kaam khatam karenge?
solution_steps_en: Step 1: Let efficiency of C = 1. Then B = 3 and A = 2 * 3 = 6.
Step 2: Total work = Efficiency of C * Days for C = 1 * 120 = 120 units.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The 'double' and 'triple' chain in Hinglish ('double hai aur B ki C se triple') often leads LLMs to apply the ratio incorrectly to time rather than efficiency, or miss the transitivity (A=6C).
why_hard: Multi-stage ratio conversion between different workers' speeds.

problem_en: A can finish a work in 18 days and B can do the same work in half the time taken by A. Then working together, what part of the same work they can finish in a day?
problem_hi: A एक काम को 18 दिनों में पूरा कर सकता है और B उसी काम को A द्वारा लिए गए समय के आधे समय में कर सकता है। फिर एक साथ काम करते हुए, वे एक दिन में उसी काम का कितना हिस्सा पूरा कर सकते हैं?
problem_hg_030: A can finish a work in 18 days and B same work A ke comparison mein half time mein karta hai. Working together, 1 day mein kitna part finish hoga?
problem_hg_065: A 18 days mein kaam khatam karta hai, par B usse 'aadhe' time mein hi kar leta hai. Agar dono mil jayein, toh ek din mein kitna kaam (fraction) 'na kam na zyada' finish hoga?
solution_steps_en: Step 2: B's time = 18/2 = 9 days. B's rate = 1/9 per day.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The phrase 'na kam na zyada' (neither less nor more) is a colloquial way to say 'exactly'. LLMs might interpret 'na...na' as a double negative or an inequality constraint rather than an equality.
why_hard: Requires calculating a reciprocal rate and identifying that the question asks for a 1-day fraction, not total days.

problem_en: If 12 men and 16 boys can do a piece of work in 5 days; 13 men and 24 boys can do it in 4 days, then how many times is the daily work of a man to that of a boy?
problem_hi: यदि 12 पुरुष और 16 लड़के एक काम को 5 दिनों में कर सकते हैं; 13 पुरुष और 24 लड़के इसे 4 दिनों में कर सकते हैं, तो एक पुरुष का दैनिक कार्य एक लड़के के कार्य का कितना गुना है?
problem_hg_030: If 12 men and 16 boys can do a work in 5 days; 13 men and 24 boys can do it in 4 days, then man ka work boy ke comparison mein kitne times hai?
problem_hg_065: 12 men aur 16 boys ne 5 din kaam kiya, aur 13 men aur 24 boys ne 4 din. Bataiye ek man ka daily work ek boy ke work se kitna 'zyada' (in ratio/times) hai?
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The word 'zyada' is used loosely to ask for the ratio ('kitna zyada' often means 'how much more' but in this context asks for the multiplier), which can confuse an LLM into performing subtraction instead of division.
why_hard: Requires formulating a comparison of work rates from two different linear combinations.

problem_en: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 20, 30 and 60 days respectively. In how many days can A do the work if he is assisted by B and C on every third day?
problem_hi: A, B और C क्रमशः 20, 30 और 60 दिनों में एक काम कर सकते हैं। A कितने दिनों में काम कर सकता है यदि उसे हर तीसरे दिन B और C द्वारा सहायता प्रदान की जाती है?
problem_hg_030: A, B and C can do work in 20, 30 and 60 days. A kitne days mein kaam karega if he is assisted by B and C on every third day?
problem_hg_065: A, B aur C ki capacity 20, 30 aur 60 days ki hai. A akela kaam shuru karta hai par 'har teesre din' use B aur C ka saath milta hai. Kaam kab khatam hoga?
solution_steps_en: Step 4: Cycles needed = 1 / (1/5) = 5 cycles. Total days = 5 * 3 = 15 days.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The phrase 'har teesre din' (every third day) is often misinterpreted as 'after three days' or 'for three days', leading to incorrect cycle summation.
why_hard: Periodic assistance creates a non-uniform work rate that must be averaged over a cycle.

problem_en: A and B undertake to do a piece of work for ₹600. A alone can do it in 6 days while B alone can do it in 8 days. With the help of C, they finish it in 3 days. Find the share of C.
problem_hi: A और B ₹600 में एक काम करने का बीड़ा उठाते हैं। A अकेले इसे 6 दिनों में कर सकता है जबकि B अकेले इसे 8 दिनों में कर सकता है। C की सहायता से, वे इसे 3 दिनों में पूरा करते हैं। C का हिस्सा ज्ञात कीजिए।
problem_hg_030: A and B undertake a work for ₹600. A can do it in 6 days, B in 8 days. With C's help, they finish in 3 days. C ka share kitna hai?
problem_hg_065: A aur B ne ₹600 ka contract liya. A ko 6 din lagte, B ko 8 din. Par C ke aane se kaam 'sirf' 3 din mein wrap up ho gaya. C ki pocket mein kitne paise jayenge?
solution_steps_en: Step 3: Share is proportional to work done. C's share = 1/8 * 600.
linguistic_trap_in_hg065: The phrase 'C ke aane se' (with C's arrival) and 'sirf 3 din' (only 3 days) might lead a model to assume C worked for a different duration or that the total time was reduced by 3 days instead of to 3 days.
why_hard: Combines work-rate calculation with wage distribution proportional to effort/part of work.
